Fetch FWA Stream Network Segments

Source: R/frs_stream_fetch.R
frs_stream_fetch.Rd

Retrieve stream segments from a stream network table. Filter by watershed group code, blue line key, bounding box and/or area of interest.

Usage

frs_stream_fetch(
  conn,
  watershed_group_code = NULL,
  blue_line_key = NULL,
  bbox = NULL,
  stream_order_min = NULL,
  table = "whse_basemapping.fwa_stream_networks_sp",
  cols = c("linear_feature_id", "blue_line_key", "waterbody_key", "edge_type",
    "gnis_name", "stream_order", "stream_magnitude", "gradient",
    "downstream_route_measure", "upstream_route_measure", "length_metre",
    "watershed_group_code", "wscode_ltree", "localcode_ltree", "geom"),
  include_all = FALSE,
  limit = NULL,
  aoi = NULL,
  simplify_m = NULL,
  order_by = "linear_feature_id"
)

Arguments

conn

A DBI::DBIConnection object (from frs_db_conn()).

watershed_group_code

Character. Watershed group code (e.g. "BULK"). Default NULL.

blue_line_key

Integer. Blue line key for a specific stream. Default NULL.

bbox

Numeric vector of length 4 (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) in BC Albers (EPSG:3005). Matches on envelope overlap (&&), so a segment whose envelope touches the box is returned even when the segment does not; use aoi for exact intersection. Default NULL.

stream_order_min

Integer. Minimum Strahler stream order to return. Default NULL (all orders).

table

Character. Fully qualified table name. Default "whse_basemapping.fwa_stream_networks_sp".

cols

Character vector of column names to select. Default includes the most commonly used FWA stream attributes.

include_all

Logical. If TRUE, include placeholder streams (999 wscode) and unmapped tributaries (NULL localcode). Default FALSE filters these out. Only applied when querying the FWA base table.

limit

Integer. Maximum rows to return. Default NULL (no limit).

aoi

Area of interest. An sf/sfc polygon (transformed to EPSG:3005, so it must carry a CRS) filters with ST_Intersects(). For WKT, pass sf::st_as_sfc(wkt, crs = 3005). Also accepts the other forms of frs_extract()'s aoi; its character form (watershed group codes) is an envelope prefilter, so use watershed_group_code to select groups. Default NULL.

simplify_m

Numeric. Simplification tolerance in metres, applied in the database. Drops M coordinates. Default NULL (full resolution).

order_by

Character vector. Columns to order rows by. Default "linear_feature_id", the FWA table's unique key; give another table's unique key (one or more columns) when table is changed, or NULL for no ORDER BY. With limit, the first limit rows in this order are returned.

Value

An sf data frame of stream segments.

Details

Rows come back ordered by order_by (the table's unique key by default), so the same database returns the same sf on every call. For map layers, simplify_m simplifies in the database with ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology(geom, simplify_m). Unlike the polygon fetchers it is not wrapped in ST_Normalize(), which would reverse any line whose first vertex sorts after its last, so segments keep their digitized (downstream to upstream) direction. length_metre is the stored, unsimplified length. Two databases on different GEOS versions can still simplify a line differently, so a caller that saves the result should record postgis_full_version() with it.

See also

Other fetch: frs_lake_fetch(), frs_wetland_fetch()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
conn <- frs_db_conn()

# All streams in the Bulkley watershed group
streams <- frs_stream_fetch(conn, watershed_group_code = "BULK")

# Streams with order >= 4
streams <- frs_stream_fetch(conn, watershed_group_code = "BULK",
  stream_order_min = 4)

# Map layer: inside a watershed polygon, simplified to 25 m
ws <- frs_watershed_at_measure(conn, 360873822, 208877, simplify_m = 25)
streams_map <- frs_stream_fetch(conn, aoi = ws, stream_order_min = 3,
  simplify_m = 25)
DBI::dbDisconnect(conn)
} # }
